Picking one stock to invest heavily in and hoping it moonshots is a straight-up bet -- and it's not advisable as a strategy, in my opinion. Diversification is smarter. Spreading your money across companies in an industry you find promising, and choosing companies that are building different pieces of the same future (space, software, silicon), is closer to a thesis and conviction that can make you some strong long-term profits.

If you're considering investing money to capitalize on the AI trend today -- say, a $10,000 total investment -- I'd suggest putting $2,000 each into these five stocks for the long term. Here's what those investments might grow into by 2035, and what each company will have to pull off to reach that potential.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
1. Space Exploration Technologies

Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX), newly public since its June 2026 IPO, trades today at around $145 per share and already has a market cap of close to $2 trillion, so the stock is widely covered.

Starlink's looming push into direct-to-cell service and Starship's path to frequent launches with cheaper costs to put payloads into space are the whole bull case with this stock. If both businesses keep compounding, a stake in the business could grow several times over by 2035. If progress with the space segment stalls, however, the stock will probably just track the market.

2. Palantir

Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) trades at around $195 currently. This year, Palantir has been turning its Ontology software, the layer connecting raw data to real decisions, into something governments and companies can't easily rip out and replace once it's embedded.

U.S. commercial revenue more than doubled in the first half of 2026, and a new partnership with Nvidia to run AI inside federal agencies suggests Palantir wants to be the operating system underneath government AI, not just a vendor to it.

For the stock to deliver on its potential, Palantir's growth rate will have to maintain its historically rare pace for years, since the current stock price already has years of enormous future success baked into it. But if the company keeps going on its current tear, a $2,000 investment made today could be worth $8,000 to $10,000 by 2035. If its growth rate cools to merely very good, I'd expect that $2,000 to grow to something closer to $3,000 over that period.

Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) took a hit from two directions late last week. Software stocks sold off together, and Bloomberg reported that Democrats, who are favored to win at least one chamber of Congress in the midterms, could aim more oversight at big tech companies, Palantir among them.

The company sells software that pulls an organization's scattered data into one place, so analysts and AI tools can act on it. Its customers are militaries and government agencies on one side and corporations on the other.

The second-quarter results were striking. Whether that's enough depends on how much of the future the price already holds, and how secure the government half of the story really is.

Palantir's Customers Are Spending Far More, Not Just Signing On

Start with the record. Revenue grew about 32.6% a year over the past five years, a strong run on its own. The second quarter blew past it: total revenue rose 93% to about $1.94 billion, and US commercial revenue jumped 149% to $764 million.

The customer count shows where that growth came from. US commercial customers rose 35% to 653, so revenue is growing far faster than the customer list. Companies already on board are spending much more.

Margins suggest buyers aren't treating the product as a commodity. Gross margin ran about 84.8% over the past 12 months, and net margin about 49%. Software that sits inside how an army or a large company operates is hard to swap out, and those margins look like what that position earns. Growth paired with a durable edge is the common thread in 10 High Growth Wide Moat Stocks to Buy.

Why Palantir (PLTR) Remains a Standout in Agentic AI at Scale
Guidance Went Up, and Analysts Have Started to Follow

Management raised its full-year outlook with the second-quarter report, guiding to about $8.15 billion in revenue, including more than $3.4 billion from US commercial customers. Third-quarter revenue is guided to about $2.16 billion, with that report due early next month.

Profitability kept pace. Adjusted operating margin was 62% in the quarter, GAAP net income was about $1.06 billion, and adjusted free cash flow reached $1.22 billion.

Wall Street has noticed. Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges upgraded the stock earlier this month, arguing the company is positioned for another phase of outperformance into 2027 and that its addressable market could step up again. Key Stats for Palantir Stock

Current Price: $186.03

Target Price (Mid): ~$1,330

Street Target: ~$206

Potential Total Return: ~613%

Annualized IRR: ~59% / year

What Happened?

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) closed at $186.03 on October 16, down 7.22%, one week after its record close of $209.05 on October 9. Shares now sit 11.01% below that record, past the 10% decline that marks a correction.

The selling hit the whole sector. During the session, 43 of 45 stocks in a Yahoo Finance software basket were falling, and the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) was down nearly 5%. Reports on the drop pointed to the software selloff and valuation worries rather than a Palantir announcement. The company's latest deal, disclosed a day earlier, and the Q2 figures in its investor relations materials say more about where revenue is heading.

Palantir Drawdowns (TIKR)
A Bank Already Working With OpenAI Added Palantir

On October 15, Customers Bank, the subsidiary of Customers Bancorp (CUBI) with nearly $27 billion in assets, announced it will deploy Palantir's Foundry and AIP for deposit onboarding. No contract value or term was disclosed, and Palantir shares traded lower that session. The bank already has a multiyear collaboration with OpenAI that also covers deposit onboarding, so Palantir enters as a second AI vendor on the same workflow.

That setup matches how management described the business on the Q2 call. D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria asked whether customers can swap models if one gets pulled. CEO Alex Karp answered: "We have a product that allows you to switch out models." In that framing, a bank that already buys from OpenAI can still become a large Palantir customer, because Palantir sells the layer that assigns models to tasks. The open question is size. This is a first workflow at a regional bank, and the release gives no sign yet of a larger contract.

Record Deal Counts Explain the 98-Times Multiple

Q2 suggests first workflows are turning into large contracts. Palantir closed 220 deals worth $1 million or more, including 73 worth $10 million or more. Chief Revenue Officer Ryan Taylor called these "record highs across the board." U.S. commercial bookings reached $2.132 billion in total contract value, nearly $800 million above the prior record quarter, according to CFO Dave Glazer. Net dollar retention of 157% shows existing customers keep spending more.

That is why Palantir still trades at a P/E of about 98 times NTM earnings after the drop. Microsoft (MSFT) trades at about 27 times, ServiceNow (NOW) at about 31 times, and SAP (SAP) at about 26 times. Revenue growth of 82%, the 2026 guidance set in August, earns a premium. But a gap that wide also means sector selloffs land hard, as October 16 showed.

title: Is Palantir Stock a Buy Right Now?

Is Palantir Stock a Buy Right Now?
Leo Sun, The Motley Fool

Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) went public through a direct listing six years ago. It started trading at $10 per share, but it's now worth about $186 per share. Let's see why this tech stock delivered such massive gains -- and if it's still worth buying today in this choppy market.

Why did Palantir's stock soar?

Palantir operates two data-aggregating platforms: Gotham for government clients and Foundry for commercial clients. Both of these platforms create "digital twins" of a client's entire organization by gathering information through databases, supply chain reports, sensors, emails, internal documents, financial records, and even social media accounts.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Palantir uses its Ontology data model to unify that fragmented data into an easy-to-query stream of information for non-technical users. Its clients can access that data to make better data-driven decisions, and it connects leading large language models (including OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude) to its platform via its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP).

Palantir's silo-busting tools are becoming essential as the AI race drives more government organizations and companies to upgrade their data mining capabilities. That's why many U.S. government agencies already use Gotham to plan their projects and missions, and why large companies like Walmart use Foundry to streamline their businesses.

Unlike many other high-growth tech companies, Palantir turned firmly profitable in 2023. It was added to the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) and the Nasdaq-100 in 2024.

From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Palantir's revenue and EPS to grow at CAGRs of 59% and 70%, respectively, as the AI market expands. Its stock isn't cheap at 87 times next year's earnings, but its explosive growth rates could justify that premium valuation.

Is Palantir's stock worth buying today?

Palantir expects global conflicts to fuel Gotham's growth through new government contracts, and the AI race to drive the expansion of its U.S. commercial business.

However, rising interest rates and Treasury yields could compress its valuation as more investors sell their higher-growth stocks to buy more conservative investments. Palantir's controversial reputation (due to its integration into immigration enforcement, mass surveillance, and military combat software) could also weigh down its stock.

Experienced investors know all too well that past performance is no guarantee of future results. Still, those same investors also know that sometimes one year's biggest winners can keep on trucking the following year.

Take artificial intelligence (AI) powerhouse Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) as an example. After soaring more than 180% in 2024, shares of the technology giant gained another 35% in 2025, and are up more than 18% so far this year. Palantir Technologies is another big name with recent back-to-back yearly wins, rallying 367% in 2024 then logging a 122% gain the following year.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Of course, these gains were driven by their underlying companies being in the right place at the right time. That's in the artificial intelligence business just as it was reaching critical mass. Plenty of red-hot tickers don't follow through.

Take Novo Nordisk as an example. Its stock was all the rage in 2023 when the company's weight-loss drug Wegovy was gaining serious traction, driving the stock more than 50% higher that year. Although it started the next year with that same bullish momentum, after peaking in mid-2024, it ended up suffering a full-year setback of more than 16% that same year, and is still losing ground.

Image source: Getty Images.

The point is, momentum alone isn't a reason to own a particular stock. There's always more to the story.

With that as the backdrop, while there's obviously no assurance that they'll do as well in 2027, here's a rundown of the best-performing stocks of the Nasdaq-100 index through Oct. 14 of this year. This index-leading bullishness is at least worth exploring.

1. Moderna

This year's best-performing Nasdaq-100 constituent is surprising in that the company isn't an AI-focused company, but rather a pharmaceutical name. The surprise is pared back, however, when you learn the stock is drugmaker Moderna (NASDAQ: MRNA). Shares are up 667% since the end of 2025, with the largest single piece of this gain materializing in mid-August in response to encouraging results from the phase 3 clinical trial of its intismeran autogene as a treatment for certain types of melanoma. That said, the FDA's approval of a flu vaccine as well as the stock's recent addition to the Nasdaq-100 index are also contributing to bullish sentiment.

Just be careful if you're counting on a repeat. Regardless of its opportunity or the R&D progress this drugmaker is making, any 667% gain achieved in less than a year is a tough act to follow, even if intismeran autogene is approved as a melanoma treatment. The stock's priced as if that approval is a foregone conclusion.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) stock trades at 78.2 times sales, compared to 3.1 for the S&P 500. Investors paying that premium need to know exactly what they are buying, and the case Palantir makes has evolved. During the fiscal Q3 2024 earnings call, executives highlighted the fast-growing number of U.S. businesses signing on as customers. By the latest call in fiscal Q2 2026, the focus had shifted. So what does management talk up now?

Palantir Now Makes The Case For Sovereign AI

By sovereign AI, Palantir means an architecture where companies maintain full control over their own data and the artificial intelligence built upon it. During the fiscal Q2 2026 call, held August 3, 2026, executives reported immense demand from enterprises for this capability. They contrasted this approach with purchasing external services from AI labs, a process they described as paying outside vendors to move proprietary corporate knowledge into third-party models.

The pitch sounded quite different during the fiscal Q3 2024 call. At that time, leadership highlighted that Palantir's U.S. commercial customer count grew to 321. Expanding that baseline served as a clear signal that more U.S. companies were adopting the software.

While Palantir still reports the customer count, the metric no longer takes center stage. Instead, the company links sovereign AI directly to increased spending per client. Customers that previously utilized only the Foundry software now want access to the broader sovereign AI stack. The core argument now rests on the size of individual customer commitments, rather than the sheer number of clients.

Shifts like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

Palantir's Business Customers Are Spending Much Larger Sums

Sales to the U.S. businesses are growing much faster than the number of businesses buying. Palantir's U.S. commercial customer count reached 653 in fiscal Q2 2026, up 35% from a year earlier. Over that same period, U.S. commercial revenue rose 149% to $764 million. These buyers belong to Palantir's commercial segment, a division that generated $2.07 billion in fiscal 2025, accounting for 46.3% of the company's total revenue that year.

Contract values follow a similar trajectory. U.S. businesses signed deals with Palantir worth $2.132 billion in total in fiscal Q2 2026, up 153% from a year earlier. Consequently, the average customer is committing significantly more capital than they were just a year ago. Executives labeled that contract total a record, forming the foundation of the case they now present.

There's always a second chance in the stock market. Investors who missed out on Apple and Amazon in the early 2000s had access to picks like Tesla and Nvidia in the 2010s. Even in this past decade, stocks like Palantir minted new millionaires.

Micron (NASDAQ: MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) have built substantial wealth for early investors over the past year. Opportunities like these will exist in the 2030s and beyond, but there's one growth stock that looks attractive right now and is riding the same tailwinds as the memory chipmakers. Here's why Penguin Solutions (NASDAQ: PENG) is worth monitoring.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
This memory play is growing faster than people realize

The front-line number, 68% year-over-year revenue growth in the company's fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, is impressive. However, the metrics are actually more compelling if you look at the company's key growth segment.

Penguin Solutions reports three segments each quarter: advanced computing, integrated memory, and optimized LED. Integrated memory is the most important segment, since it includes key memory products for AI data centers. Its DRAM modules are the top seller, while Penguin Solutions' CXL memory modules are surging in demand as a recognized solution to the memory wall bottleneck.

CXL enables GPUs to access a memory pool. Without this setup, a single AI chip can crash or slow down an AI model if it runs out of memory. Since CXL solves this problem and Penguin Solutions is one of the few companies already delivering this technology, it has a massive tailwind.

These trends helped Penguin Solutions' integrated memory segment grow by 158% year over year. It grew much faster than the other two segments and made up 60% of overall sales. As the memory segment grows and accounts for a larger share of total revenue, Penguin Solutions' revenue and net income growth rates should continue to accelerate.

Penguin Solutions is winning more customers

While consumer-facing companies like Walmart must consistently win over many customers, Penguin Solutions only needs a handful to generate substantial revenue growth. That's why it was such a big deal when the company won six new AI infrastructure data center customers in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.

That customer profile included four neocloud providers, which must aggressively scale out data centers to deliver for customers. The data center scale-out will increase demand for Penguin Solutions' memory products, especially its CXL products that address the memory wall.

Orders Galore For RTX's Raytheon

Raytheon, RTX's unit, announced $729 million in contracts to supply components of its LIDS counter-drone system to the U.S. Army, Qatar and Jordan. The system combines KuRFS radar, which detects and tracks incoming drones, with Coyote interceptors designed to destroy individual drones and swarms.

The agreements mark the first international sales of both KuRFS and Coyote. RTX said it is increasing Coyote production to meet growing demand.

Separately, Raytheon won a contract from the Office of Naval Research (ONR) to develop advanced target‑detection capabilities for naval radar systems. On Thursday, Raytheon was selected to modernize U.S. Space Force radar sites to improve early warnings of missile launches, identify object types, and track activities in space.

L3Harris, HII Land New Military Orders

L3Harris Technologies (LHX) received a $250 million follow-on contract from Lockheed Martin (LMT) to manufacture propulsion systems for Guided Multiple Launch Rocket System rockets.

The company also won a $55 million U.S. Army contract to supply NOVA binocular night-vision goggles.

Meanwhile, shipbuilder HII secured a $56 million U.S. Navy contract for engineering and design support under the AUKUS submarine partnership.

AeroVironment Expands International Drone Partnerships

AeroVironment (AVAV) announced four international partnerships this week, covering drone manufacturing, integration and communications technology.

The company signed an agreement with Australia's NIOA to explore production of one-way attack drones. It also partnered with Taiwan's Thunder Tiger on potential drone co-production and integration.

AeroVironment also signed agreements with Spain's Alpha Unmanned Systems for maintenance, training and technical support for AVAV's JUMP 20 surveillance drones and with Israel's Elsight, which will provide communications technology for the Mayhem 10 drone system.
